definition: The screen area that displays a web document. The area used to calculate layout can differ from the area actually visible depending on factors such as zoom and the keyboard.
example: Check that the input field and buttons are not hidden in the mobile viewport.

definition: A recording method or data that preserves the information captured by a camera sensor in a form prior to final image processing.
example: Check the exposure and color processing settings during RAW development.
note: Log is a way of representing the signal, while RAW concerns the processing and recording form of sensor information. Do not conflate the two as the same file type.

definition: A code that identifies the temporal position of video or audio using values such as hours, minutes, seconds, and frames.
example: Deliver the original footage together with its timecode information to the editing team.
note: It does not always match the absolute time of an actual clock. You must align criteria such as the frame rate and whether drop-frame is used.

definition: A stage or edit in which the cut lengths, transitions, and rhythm are finely refined from an edit whose overall structure is already set.
example: In the fine cut, adjust the pacing of the pauses between lines of dialogue.
note: The distinction between rough and final edits differs by team. Do not assume it is the same as the final delivery version with color grading, sound, and compositing completed.

definition: The work of analyzing the movement of feature points or regions within footage to track changes such as position and rotation.
example: Use motion tracking to match graphics to the movement of a sign.
note: Distinguish it from tracking shots where the camera moves to follow a subject. Here it means image analysis in post-production.

definition: The work of designating an area so that only part of the frame is visible or to limit the range to which an effect is applied.
example: Use masking to define the area on the face where correction will be applied.

definition: The visual impression of footage created by color, contrast, texture, and so on, or the direction of that expression.
example: Match the look to a reference, then adjust it scene by scene.
note: This is the context of a video's visual expression. Do not automatically equate it with look and feel, which also includes the operational feel of an interface.

definition: The process of making garment samples before mass production to check and adjust design, fit, material, sewing, and so on.
example: Revise the work order to reflect the sampling results.

definition: The cost set as compensation for performing agreed work such as sewing or processing.
example: Check the scope of work included in the labor cost and any additional processing fees.

definition: Mixing different types of fibers to form yarn or fabric.
example: Check the fiber types and ratios of the blended fabric.
note: Distinguish it from union weaving, which combines different yarns as warp and weft.

definition: A direction diagonal to the warp and weft of a fabric. True bias, at 45 degrees to each of the two directions, is used in cutting that takes advantage of drape and stretch.
example: After bias cutting, check the stretch and trim the length.

definition: A printing method that transfers a pattern prepared on paper or film onto fabric or a garment using conditions such as heat and pressure.
example: Check the fabric and work conditions suited to the transfer method.
note: The transfer principle of ink, dye, film, and so on differs by method. Sublimation transfer is one type of transfer printing, and not all transfers are sublimation.

definition: A design in which the shoulder line where the sleeve attaches is set lower than the natural shoulder point.
example: Check the sleeve length of the drop shoulder while it is worn.

definition: The work of temporarily fixing the position or shape of fabric with provisional stitches before the main sewing.
example: Baste to set the position, then proceed with the main sewing.
note: The submitted word 'simchimi' was not adopted as a sewing headword. Basting is used in fitting, but it is not the same as the entire fitting stage.

definition: The number of sewing stitches that fit within a set length. SPI means stitches per inch.
example: Set the stitch count to suit the fabric and the sewing purpose.
note: A higher stitch count is not unconditionally better sewing. Set it according to the fabric, thread, needle, and sewing purpose.

definition: A central phrase crafted to convey the core message of an advertisement or campaign to consumers. It is used as the standard for setting the expressive direction of various creative assets.
example: Decide the campaign key copy first, then adapt it for banners and videos.
note: The key message is the core content to be conveyed, and the key copy expresses it as ad copy. It can be used as a headline or slogan, but it is not always the same concept. The scope of use for the main copy may differ by company.

definition: A defect in which the bond between the fusible interlining and the outer fabric weakens or detaches, causing the surface to bubble up. Distinguish it from a fit problem where the garment lifts away from the body when worn.
example: Interlining lifting appeared on the front panel after washing, so check the bonding conditions and material compatibility.
note: Do not determine the cause from visible bubbles alone. Inspect the material, bonding conditions, finishing, and washing conditions together.

definition: An explanatory structure that connects the problems found in research and consumer understanding to strategy, concept, and execution, convincing others why this advertising should be done.
example: The idea is good, but please strengthen the logic that connects it to the problem analysis up front.
note: In advertising planning it refers to the persuasion that leads from research to strategy and idea; in general business it explains the grounds and conclusion of a judgment. Processing rules in development are covered under the logic (code) entry.

definition: In an advertising proposal, the part that analyzes background, market, consumers, and problems and builds the basis for strategy before presenting the full concept or execution plan.
example: The front end raised a pricing problem, but the later campaign idea talks about awareness, so they do not connect.
note: It is not a fixed process name or page range. State what it is the front part of. Check the explanation by field.

definition: The term for the later part of a proposal that develops the previously presented analysis and strategy into concrete concept, deliverables, media operation, schedule, and so on.
example: The target definition in the front end must carry through to the media and execution plan in the back end.
note: It is not a fixed process name or page range. State what it is the back part of.

definition: Specifying, based on research and business goals, what consumer perception or behavior the campaign needs to change.
example: If awareness is high but purchases are low, reconsider whether the problem should be defined as a lack of awareness.

definition: Conveying a product or message attractively by appealing to consumers' interest, desires, emotions, and so on.
example: Rather than listing features, appeal to the time saved while using it.

definition: The appeal or reason emphasized in advertising to get consumers interested or to choose the product.
example: Set the appeal point of this ad as ease of use rather than low price.
note: It means the reason emphasized in advertising and does not necessarily match the USP, a unique strength that competitors lack.

definition: The sequence of a proposal structured so that analysis, insight, strategy, and idea connect into a single persuasive flow.
example: Before designing the slides, read just the titles in sequence to check the storyline.

definition: A central creative idea that can bind and extend the various media and executions of a campaign into one.
example: Check whether this big idea extends beyond the TV ad to in-store events as well.

definition: The creative work, or its output, concerning what idea and expression will be used to convey an advertisement's message.
example: Keeping the strategy, split the creative into a humor-focused version and a plain version.

definition: A metaphor for the decisive element in an advertising idea or expression that grabs attention and makes it memorable.
example: The overall flow makes sense, but it lacks a memorable kick at the end.
note: It is a metaphorical expression used in idea reviews. Not every company calls the same element a kick, so specify what to strengthen.

definition: The relationship and way of development that explains how the premise, grounds, and conclusion of a judgment or proposal connect.
example: Please explain the logic of how the conclusion that costs will decrease was derived.
note: In advertising planning it refers to the persuasion that leads from research to strategy and idea; in general business it explains the grounds and conclusion of a judgment. Processing rules in development are covered under the logic (code) entry.

definition: A condition or assumption set as the starting point of a judgment or plan.
example: The premise that staff would be added has changed, so let's review the schedule again.

definition: The facts, data, or reasons presented to support a claim or judgment.
example: Please attach demand changes and cost data as grounds for the opinion that the budget should be increased.

definition: The background and surrounding circumstances needed to understand the meaning of a statement or judgment.
example: If you share the context in which this revision request arose, it will be easier to set the scope.

definition: The necessity and legitimate reason explaining why a particular proposal or task must be done.
example: There is an explanation that we can do it, but we need more on why it must be done now.

definition: A public reason for explaining an action or proposal to stakeholders and gaining acceptance.
example: Beyond simple cost reduction, make clear the rationale of improving customer inconvenience.

definition: The central issue that must be judged or agreed on in a discussion.
example: Rather than design taste, today's point of discussion is how far the delivery scope should go.

definition: A state in which the explanation or evidence needed to move from premise or grounds to conclusion is missing.
example: Concluding the preference of all customers from the opinions of a few respondents is a logical leap.

definition: A tentative explanation set up and to be verified in order to explain an observed phenomenon or predict a result.
example: Set up the hypothesis that long guidance text increases inquiries, and compare.

definition: The core content of a proposal or document excluding the details.
example: Please share the gist of the proposal in three sentences first.

definition: The overall concept that considers goals, structure, priorities, and relationships together before deciding individual tasks.
example: Before getting into the detailed schedule, let's align on the big picture of overall goals and roles.

definition: The goal or orientation used as the standard for choices and judgments while carrying out work.
example: Even with several options, maintain the direction of prioritizing ease of use over cost.

definition: A framework that structures a story or explanation into introduction, development, turn, and conclusion.
example: Review the narrative structure of the presentation and fix the part that ends without a conclusion.
note: Not every proposal must follow this order. A structure that delivers the conclusion first is also used.

definition: The relationship or explanation that makes preceding and following claims or content flow naturally.
example: Please add one more slide explaining the link between the customer research results and the proposal.

definition: A business term for a single screen or page of presentation or report material. Depending on context, it can also refer to a set of such pages collectively.
example: On this slide, please keep only one conclusion and its supporting grounds.

definition: A term referring to which words and sentences were used to express the same content.
example: Please change the wording of the notice so it does not read as if it is already confirmed.

definition: The detailed material or source data that supports the figures and claims in a report or proposal.
example: Along with the summary slide, please prepare the backup data for checking the calculation basis.
note: This is the context of supporting material for reports and proposals. It differs from data backup, which is replicated for disaster recovery.

definition: The processing rules and sequence of a program that performs calculation, judgment, state changes, and so on according to input and conditions.
example: Because the amount changes if the order of applying discounts and coupons differs, check the payment logic.
note: This means the rules and processing flow that software actually executes. Distinguish it from the logical argument used to persuade a proposal.

definition: A relative term for the part that receives or processes requests and data earlier than a given function or component used as the reference.
example: Validate the input format on the front side before sending the request to the server, but keep server validation too.
note: It means a relative processing position. Do not always equate the front side with the frontend; confirm the target and reference such as browser, gateway, or preprocessing.

definition: A relative term for the part that takes over and processes requests and data behind a given function or component used as the reference.
example: After the API accepts the task, check whether the actual processing completes in the back-side task queue.
note: It means a relative processing position. Do not always equate the back side with the backend; confirm the target and reference such as follow-up functions, queues, or services.

definition: A relative term for the beginning side of the video or segment being edited.
example: The interview at the front part runs long, so show the key remark first and move the background explanation later.
note: It is colloquial for the beginning side of a video or editing segment. It does not mean the same as pre-production, the preparation stage before shooting.

definition: A relative term for the ending side of the video or segment being edited.
example: The same explanation repeats at the back part, so trim the two cuts just before the ending.
note: It is colloquial for the ending side of a video or editing segment. It does not mean the same as the entire post-production process.

definition: The developmental flow in which events, characters, and information connect in a video to form the overall story.
example: Check whether the storyline still flows naturally after changing the interview order.

definition: The reason behind choices of form, layout, color, and so on based on goals, users, brand, and production conditions, and the effect intended to be conveyed.
example: Explain the design intent that the title was enlarged for information priority, not decoration.

definition: A short communication or meeting to check and align differences in progress, understanding, schedule, and so on among stakeholders.
example: Let's sync up on the changed scope before tomorrow's client meeting.

definition: A process of briefly confirming participants' situations, progress, and where they need help at the start or middle of a meeting.
example: Before the main agenda, let's check in on whether anyone is stuck.

definition: A method of setting a time limit in advance for a discussion or task, or that time interval itself.
example: Let's discuss this agenda item in a 15-minute timebox and organize the remaining issues separately.

definition: A list or method of separately noting topics that are off the current discussion or hard to decide immediately, to revisit later.
example: Leave the separate budget discussion in the parking lot and set a time to revisit it with the owner.
note: It does not mean forgetting the deferred item. Record the time to revisit it and who is responsible.

definition: Content that strays from the current agenda or purpose of discussion.
example: That suggestion is off-topic for today's agenda, so let's set a separate meeting.

definition: A meeting where participants jointly create documents, drafts, or solutions rather than merely sharing status.
example: In the working session to organize the scope, let's create the task list by owner together.

definition: Material shared to be read in advance of a meeting so participants understand the context and issues.
example: Mark the three decision questions in the pre-read before sending it.

definition: Material that summarizes the purpose, key content, and needed decisions within a single page.
example: Summarize the cost and expected effect on the one-pager so reviewers can judge quickly.

definition: The specific tasks and order to follow after a meeting or task.
example: Before ending the meeting, assign owners and deadlines for the next steps.

definition: A matter that still needs further confirmation or discussion because no answer or decision has been reached.
example: Leave the quote's scope of inclusion as an open issue and confirm it with the purchasing team.

definition: The content that stakeholders participating in the discussion have agreed to accept together.
example: In the minutes, distinguish the agreed items from content requiring additional approval.

definition: A record kept so that decisions made, along with their reasons, dates, and involved parties, can be traced.
example: Check the decision log for the reason the scope was reduced earlier.

definition: A person with the authority and responsibility to make the final choice or approval on a particular matter.
example: Before gathering opinions, confirm who the decision-maker for this budget is.

definition: A person or organization that influences, or is affected by the outcome of, a task or decision.
example: The operations team is also a stakeholder affected by the change, so include them in the review.

definition: A role that helps the process so participants contribute opinions on purpose and keep the discussion moving.
example: The facilitator manages speaking time and organizes the remaining issues.

definition: A state in which stakeholders understand the necessity and direction of a proposal and support and participate in it.
example: Before execution, explain the burden and the effect together to gain the operations owner's buy-in.

definition: A problem or condition that blocks the next task or progress until it is resolved.
example: Unconfirmed delivery specifications are a blocker, so get the owner's confirmation first.

definition: Raising a problem that is hard to resolve within the current scope to a person with greater authority or relevant responsibility to request judgment or support.
example: The cross-department schedule conflict is not resolving, so escalate it to the person in charge.

definition: A relationship in which improving one condition requires giving up or reducing another.
example: Compare the trade-off between launch timing and feature scope, then decide.

definition: The order in which multiple tasks should be handled first according to importance, urgency, dependencies, and so on.
example: Set priority by customer impact and deadline rather than request order.

definition: A task or result that yields visible improvement with relatively small input or in a short time.
example: Before the big overhaul, start with fixing the guidance text as a quick win.

definition: The size and nature of the effect a task or decision has on customers, performance, cost, operations, and so on.
example: Compare not only the workload but also the impact of how much customer inconvenience will be reduced.

definition: A state of progressing in line with the agreed plan or goal.
example: The key deliverables are coming out as scheduled, so the current timeline is on track.

definition: A state of deviating from the agreed schedule or goal and needing adjustment.
example: The review is delayed and the schedule is off track, so let's make a recovery plan.

definition: The slack left in schedule, resources, and so on to absorb unexpected delays or fluctuations.
example: Allow a two-day buffer considering the time external inspection may take.
note: It means slack in work schedule or resources. Distinguish it from a buffer, the temporary storage space in a program.

definition: The task path that determines the overall completion time when considering the sequence and durations of a project.
example: An approval on the critical path is delayed, which may push back the overall delivery date.

definition: A specific difficulty or inconvenience a customer or user experiences in the process of achieving a goal.
example: Having to contact several people repeatedly is a pain point in the intake process.

definition: The goal set for what change to create in the target's awareness, understanding, attitude, or behavior through advertising.
example: Separate from the sales goal, set a communication objective of informing people about the new usage.

definition: The direction that decides who to deliver what message to, through which touchpoints and methods, to create the intended change.
example: Separate the communication strategy for repeat customers and first-time customers.

definition: An understanding found in the target consumer's behavior, desires, and tensions, used as the starting point for advertising strategy and expression.
example: Review the target insight that the reason for hesitating to buy is not price but anxiety about failure.

definition: The evidence and reasons presented so consumers can believe an advertisement's promise or product claim.
example: Check what reason to believe will be presented for the copy that promises an effect.
note: Even within advertising, RTB can mean real-time bidding in ad trading. Check from context whether it is the basis of a strategy or media bidding.

definition: The degree to which an idea, model, collaboration, or expression suits the brand's identity and direction.
example: The buzz is high, but separately review whether the model is a brand fit.

definition: The degree to which a message, expression, or medium matches the target consumer's situation and interests.
example: Look at the actual customers' target fit first, rather than the copy the team likes.

definition: A structure that divides content to be conveyed in advertising by importance and decides which message is shown or remembered first.
example: Set the message hierarchy so the product name and the benefit do not compete.

definition: The process of reviewing whether advertising ideas and drafts fit the strategy, brand, and media conditions, and deciding the revision direction.
example: In the creative review, discuss based on the brief's goals rather than personal taste.

definition: An explanation of the problem awareness behind creating this campaign and what it aims to convey to or change in consumers.
example: Check whether the planning intent is maintained even when the expression changes.

definition: An idea draft that simply shows only the core concept before finished copy or drafts.
example: Pick from three rough ideas' concepts first, then develop the selected one.

definition: Checking and adjusting so that the advertising spend is used at the targeted pace and proportion over the run period.
example: Check the budget pacing so the budget is not front-loaded early in the month.

definition: The phenomenon where interest or response declines from repeated exposure to the same advertising expression.
example: Frequency is high and click response is dropping, so suspect creative fatigue.
note: Do not conclude that the cause of a performance drop is fatigue. Also check factors such as bidding, targeting, measurement, and seasonality.

definition: The difference or increase showing how much a metric such as awareness or conversion rose compared with a baseline group or comparison condition.
example: When reporting lift, specify whether it is the absolute difference from a comparison group or a relative increase rate.
note: The calculation method differs by metric and comparison design. A simple before-and-after increase does not confirm a causal effect.

definition: A group deliberately not exposed to the advertising or treatment, kept as a comparison baseline.
example: Compare the holdout and exposed groups to examine the campaign's incremental effect.

definition: The result that occurred additionally because of advertising, compared with not advertising.
example: Check the comparison design so you do not count all ad-attributed sales as incremental effect.

definition: The process of reviewing campaign results and causes against goals and deciding what to keep or change in the next run.
example: In the performance review, check not only the good creatives but also missing conversion tracking.

definition: A Scrum event that defines the sprint goal, the work to be done, and the plan to carry it out.
example: In sprint planning, check the work needed for the goal together with available time.

definition: A Scrum event where the sprint results and progress toward the goal are examined with stakeholders and the next work is adjusted.
example: In the sprint review, look at the actual behavior and user response to discuss the next direction.
note: Do not treat it only as a simple demo or final approval gate. Review results and environmental changes together and adjust the next direction.

definition: The ongoing activity of breaking backlog items into smaller, clearer pieces and specifying descriptions, order, size, and so on.
example: In refinement, split the vague order-cancellation requirement by condition.
note: It is an ongoing activity and is not defined as a separate mandatory Scrum event.

definition: The process of technically examining how to implement requirements and the constraints, risks, and operational burden.
example: In the technical review, check the compatibility and maintenance burden of the new library.

definition: The process of reviewing before implementation whether the design of components, data, interfaces, failure handling, and so on satisfies the requirements.
example: In the design review, check what state the data is left in when payment fails.

definition: A document that records important design decisions along with their background, alternatives, reasons for the choice, and impact.
example: Record the reason for choosing a synchronous call and its constraints as an ADR.

definition: A standard the team agrees on for how much requirements, dependencies, verification conditions, and so on must be prepared before starting work.
example: Per the DoR, check that the acceptance criteria and required APIs are organized.
note: It is the team's work-readiness standard. It is not an official artifact mandated by the Scrum Guide.

definition: Work that investigates or experiments with an uncertain technical problem or approach in a short, limited scope.
example: Since accurate effort estimation is hard, confirm the integration feasibility with a half-day spike.
note: It is investigative work limited by time and learning goal. It does not necessarily produce a completed product feature.

definition: A case where input, state, or environment lies at a boundary or rare condition and may behave differently from the normal flow.
example: Also review edge cases such as a zero amount or a session that just expired.

definition: The representative success flow that proceeds with expected input and order without errors or exceptions.
example: Do not just check the happy path; also test payment cancellation and retry.

definition: Handling that detects errors or conditions outside the normal flow and determines recovery, notification, halting, and so on.
example: In the timeout exception handling, check that no duplicate payment occurs.

definition: An alternative behavior applied when the original function or path is unavailable.
example: Add a fallback that shows the default list when the recommendation API fails.

definition: The property by which a new version continues to support the data, interfaces, and usage of the previous version.
example: When changing the API response, check backward compatibility with the old app version.

definition: A change that may prevent existing users or integration code from continuing to work without modification.
example: Check with the client whether adding a required field is a breaking change.

definition: The property that repeating the same request or operation produces the same intended effect as performing it once.
example: Design idempotency so that retrying a payment does not create a duplicate order.
note: It does not mean the response content or response code of repeated requests must always be identical.

definition: A state in which the relationships and values among data conform to defined rules and do not contradict each other.
example: Check the data integrity between order status and payment records.

definition: The scope of functions and systems whose behavior may change or where problems may arise due to code, configuration, or data changes.
example: Check the impact scope of changing the shared authentication module and decide the regression test targets.

definition: The process of applying or releasing a new feature or version to users, environments, and so on in stages.
example: Roll out to internal users first, check the error rate, then widen the scope.

definition: A plan that defines the conditions, procedures, and responsibilities for reverting to the previous state if a deployment or change has problems.
example: Check the rollback plan for whether even data changes can be reverted.

definition: A state or rule that restricts code changes during a set period for release stabilization and so on.
example: After the code freeze, only approved emergency fixes are applied.

definition: The process of determining reproducibility, severity, priority, ownership, and handling direction for reported bugs.
example: In bug triage, we decided to handle the data-loss issue first.

definition: A session to review developed garment samples together for design, fit, material, price, and sales potential, and decide on revisions or adoption.
example: In the product review meeting, compare by outfit, then separate the jackets to adopt from the pants to revise.

definition: The overall composition of items and styles developed together in a season or collection.
example: Seeing the outerwear-heavy lineup, reinforce the inner items.

definition: The number of distinct garment designs planned or operated. Distinguish it from the number of SKUs by color and size combination.
example: Keep the number of styles and reduce the number of colors to adjust inventory burden.

definition: The composition deciding what proportion and role of items such as tops, bottoms, and outerwear to carry.
example: Seeing seasonal demand, increase the proportion of lightweight outerwear in the item composition.

definition: The combination and proportion of product categories, price ranges, styles, and so on that a brand will carry.
example: Review the product mix of basic items and seasonal statement products.
